title: Children’s Safety and Well-Being in the Age of AI: Best Practices and Incentives
gist: Short WEF report summary (176 words) arguing that generative, conversational and agentic AI amplify risks to children via personalization, persuasion, memory and autonomy, and proposing life-cycle best practices plus incentive levers (regulation, procurement, assurance, investment, shared infrastructure, accountability) to drive implementation. Only the landing-page abstract is available, not the full PDF.

insights.claim: The World Economic Forum argues that generative, conversational and agentic AI can introduce or intensify risks to children through personalization, persuasion, memory and increasingly autonomous action.
insights.speaker: World Economic Forum
insights.so_what: Persuasion, memory and autonomy features in consumer AI products are the specific capabilities likely to attract child-safety scrutiny and compliance cost.
